claims.text: Targeted chemical substitution in non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys can tune magnetic behavior.
Targeted chemical substitution can change the magnetic ordering temperature.
Changing the magnetic ordering temperature through substitution modifies the magnetocaloric effect.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA has a single-phase microstructure.
The proposed intervention is partial replacement of one or more transition-metal elements.
Using identical melting and annealing conditions isolates the effect of chemical substitution.
The substituted samples can retain a single-phase microstructure.
Chemical substitution changes local atomic environments.
Chemical substitution changes magnetic exchange interactions.
Changes in local atomic environments and exchange interactions alter magnetic anisotropy and magnetic ordering.
Changing the balance of magnetic exchange interactions modifies the magnetic moment.
Changing the balance of magnetic exchange interactions modifies the magnetic ordering temperature.
Changes in magnetic moment and ordering temperature adjust the magnitude and temperature range of the magnetocaloric effect.
An optimally substituted alloy will have a shifted magnetic ordering temperature relative to the original alloy.
An optimally substituted alloy will exhibit an enhanced magnetocaloric effect relative to the original alloy.
The proposed tuning strategy applies only within a compositional regime that retains a single-phase HEA structure.
